page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a single dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, complemented by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 2.0 GB, maintaining a strict 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio characteristic of compute-oriented profiles. The instance includes hardware AES cryptographic support but does not include local instance storage or bundled GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and standard network interfaces offering a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the strengths and limitations of its single-core configuration. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs strongly at 14.17 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems, while single-threaded gzip compression achieves an average 29.99 GB/sec. The stress-ng single-core result reaches 1694.69 points, falling into the middle 50% tier. However, because aggregate throughput is constrained by the presence of only a single core, multi-threaded metrics such as PassMark overall score (988.37) and stress-ng multi-core fall into the lower tiers. Memory bandwidth tests measure 30.4 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 12.07 GB/sec for uncached writes, while Redis operations reach 2.4 million SET commands per second.

The primary tradeoff of the c8gn.medium lies in its lightweight resource envelope versus the per-core efficiency of modern ARM Neoverse-V2 silicon. While it lacks the absolute throughput needed for heavy multi-threaded processing or large-scale data caches, it provides cost-effective dedicated compute capability without CPU credit limits or burst exhaustion. This profile makes it well aligned for lightweight microservices, small API routers, edge ingestion tasks, single-threaded batch transformations, and entry-level container deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gn.medium is a compact compute-optimized instance driven by an ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V2 core operating at 2.8 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 1 dedicated vCPU and 2.0 GB of memory, it delivers a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio without integrated GPU acceleration or local disk storage. The instance features hardware AES acceleration, a 36 MB L3 cache, and a 3 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance in specific compression tasks, such as bzip3 decompression at 14.17 GB/sec, alongside middle-tier stress-ng single-core execution. Because overall processing capacity is strictly bounded by its single-core design, multi-core and memory-heavy benchmarks occupy the lower percentile tiers. The hardware configuration offers cost efficiency for single-threaded or low-concurrency operations, serving well as a platform for lightweight containerized microservices, small backend workers, utility scripts, and entry-level networking components.
